title: Fulmali Scored an Unbeaten Fifty. Radha and Shreyanka Took Seven Wickets Between Them. India's T20 World Cup Has Begun.
excerpt: The reigning ODI World Cup champions beat West Indies by 26 runs in their opening warm-up in Cardiff. India play Pakistan in the tournament proper on June 14.
body:
Fulmali Scored an Unbeaten Fifty. Radha and Shreyanka Took Seven Wickets Between Them. India's T20 World Cup Has Begun.

India's women began their T20 World Cup campaign exactly the way they wanted: with a win, runs from the top order, and their spinners making the ball talk on English soil. Harmanpreet Kaur's squad beat West Indies by 26 runs in their opening warm-up match at Sophia Gardens, Cardiff, on Monday.

Batting first, Smriti Mandhana -- captaining the side for this fixture -- and Shafali Verma gave India a flying start. The pair put on 59 for the first wicket before Aaliyah Alleyne broke through, having Mandhana mistime a shot to mid-on for 39 off 23 balls. The southpaw struck eight fours in an innings that set the tone for everything that followed.

India raced to 70 for 1 in the powerplay, but a cluster of three quick wickets threatened to slow them down. That is when Bharti Fulmali stepped up.

Fulmali Holds the Innings Together

The 22-year-old from Maharashtra had already caught the eye with her composure in domestic cricket. On Monday, she showed it on the international stage. Partnering first with Yastika Bhatia -- who scored a fluent 36 off 26 before being retired out to give others match time -- and then shepherding the tail, Fulmali finished unbeaten on 56 off 40 balls. Her innings included six fours and the only six of India's innings. She took India from a wobble at 133 for 5 to a competitive 179 for 8.

Afy Fletcher was the standout bowler for West Indies, claiming 4 for 23 from her four overs of leg-break.

Spinners Seal It

Chasing 180, West Indies started with intent. Deandra Dottin and Shemaine Campbelle put on 63 for the opening wicket. But the required rate climbed -- they managed only 37 in the powerplay -- and once Campbelle was retired out, the innings fell apart.

Shreyanka Patil and Radha Yadav did the damage. Patil claimed 4 for 36 with her left-arm spin, while Yadav took 3 for 25. Between them, they accounted for all seven wickets that fell. Dottin fell agonisingly short of a half-century, dismissed for 49 off 41 balls, and the rest of the lineup could not keep pace. West Indies finished on 153 for 8.

The Road to June 14

India have one more warm-up fixture -- against hosts England on June 10 in Cardiff -- before the main tournament begins. Their opening group match is against Pakistan on June 14 at Edgbaston, a fixture that carries weight far beyond the points table.

The squad Harmanpreet leads into this World Cup is arguably India's strongest ever in the T20 format. They arrive as the reigning ODI World Cup champions after beating South Africa in last year's final, and the confidence from that triumph is palpable. This success not only boosts the morale of players but also strengthens the ties of the Indian diaspora, who take pride in their national team's achievements abroad.

"We have seen that during last year's World Cup when we won, many girls started coming to play cricket," Harmanpreet said at the captains' press conference. "When we do well, a lot of things change."

Where NRIs Can Watch

The warm-up matches are available free on ICC.tv and the ICC's official YouTube channel in most regions. In India, coverage is on Star Sports and JioHotstar. For fans in the US and Canada, Willow TV carries all matches including the warm-ups.

The main tournament schedule for India: Pakistan (June 14, Edgbaston), Netherlands (June 17, Headingley), South Africa (June 21, Old Trafford), and Bangladesh (June 25, Old Trafford). If India tops their group, a semi-final at The Oval on June 30 awaits. The final is at Lord's on July 5.

For the Indian diaspora in the UK, this is a rare chance to watch the Women in Blue in person. Tickets are available through the ICC's official portal, and venues across England -- from Birmingham to London to Leeds to Manchester -- will host matches through the first week of July. This opportunity not only allows fans to support their team live but also strengthens the cultural connections among NRIs, fostering a sense of community and pride in their heritage.
